result.title: SEE: Unlocking the Hidden Perception of Frozen VLMs
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) grasp the overall content of an image but often miss the fine details a question hinges on, such as a small object in a large photo or a number in a dense infographic. Yet even when their answer is wrong, the region they point to often contains the evidence. We introduce Self-Elicited Evidence (SEE), a training-free method that lets a frozen VLM look again where it points. When the initial answer has low confidence, SEE prompts the model to propose regions where the details may appear, answers the question on these enlarged crops, and aggregates the answers with the original prediction through confidence-weighted voting. The model also answers with its own transcript, which helps on text-rich images. SEE needs no detector or OCR engine. Across five backbones, SEE improves every small-object benchmark by 2.3-13.1 points and outperforms five training-free baselines on small objects. With SEE, Qwen3.5-4B surpasses the direct answer of Qwen3.5-9B and matches the 6 times larger Qwen3.5-27B.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出无需训练的 SEE：当冻结 VLM 初次作答置信度低时，让模型自行指出细节可能所在的区域，在放大裁剪上重答，并以置信度加权投票融合原答案，同时利用模型自生成转写辅助文本密集图像。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“指向区域常含证据”的诊断与置信度触发的再查看，直接关联 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、LOOK 收益成本与停止决策；可作为无 latent 状态生成路线的对照基线，但需核查其增益是否源于裁剪放大而非证据定位能力。
